Indian vulture.fact: Based on nuclear and mitochondrial DNA evidence, it was separated into a different species from the Indian vulture in 2001.  == Distribution and habitat == The range of the Indian vulture extended from southeastern Pakistan to south India and to Indochina and the northern Malay Peninsula in the east.  It is now extinct in South East Asia with current populations existing mostly in central and peninsular India, south of the Gangetic plains.  It is also found in southwest Pakistan, Bangladesh and Nepal.  It is also found in various land-forms ranging from semi-desert to dry foot hills, open fields and cultivable lands near villages, near garbage dumps and slaughter houses in urban areas.  They are not migratory but travel hundreds of miles in a day scavenging for food.  Indian vultures nest on cliffs or high buildings and rarely on trees

It reaches speeds of 35 km/h (22 mph) when gliding and can fly for six to seven hours continuously.  The Indian vulture nests mainly on cliffs and is usually found is small flocks, sometimes with other vulture species.  === Diet and feeding === The Indian vulture is a keystone species in its habitats and is a scavenging bird, feeding mostly from carcasses of dead animals.  It plays a crucial role in the ecosystem by removing rotting meat that would otherwise spread disease

A platform of sticks or twigs lined with leaves with the addition of green leaves advertising nest occupancy and fend off parasites.  Indian vultures reach breeding age at about five years old.  Nest building starts in September and breeding happens between November and March.  They often breed in monogamous pairs and the females lay only one egg a year.  The egg is pure white or mottled with rusty spots.  Both the parents take turns in incubating the egg and the egg hatches in about 50 days

The nests are located at higher altitudes with nearly 90% of the nests at an altitude of more than 900m.  == Status and conservation == === Population decline and recovery === Beginning in the 1990s, the Indian vulture species suffered a 97% population decrease in its range in the Indian subcontinent over a period of 10–15 years. Insubres.fact: Polybius lists them along the Po after the Laevi and Libici and before the Cenomani, and calls them the most powerful of the Cisalpine Gauls. Their frontier with the Cenomani probably ran along the Oglio in the 3rd century BC.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: After the Roman conquest it was brought back westward to the Adda, to the advantage of the colony of _____
Insubres.fact: After the Roman conquest it was brought back westward to the Adda, to the advantage of the colony of Cremona.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: Ermanno A. Arslan questions whether the populations of the lower _____ and the Varese region were Insubrian at all, treating the area as a frontier rather than Insubrian land proper
Insubres.fact: Ermanno A. Arslan questions whether the populations of the lower Lake Maggiore and the Varese region were Insubrian at all, treating the area as a frontier rather than Insubrian land proper.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: A surplus population of Gauls led by _____ crossed the Alps by the passes of the Taurini, defeated the Etruscans near the Ticino, and founded Mediolanum in the ager Insubrius
Insubres.fact: A surplus population of Gauls led by Bellovesus crossed the Alps by the passes of the Taurini, defeated the Etruscans near the Ticino, and set up Mediolanum in the ager Insubrius.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: No archaeological trace of intrusive groups, of the kind found east of the _____ and south of the Po, has been identified in their territory
Insubres.fact: No archaeological trace of intrusive groups, of the kind found east of the Oglio and south of the Po, has been identified in their territory.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: The same continuity underlies the reconstruction of _____, who treats the La Tène migration into Italy as selective
Insubres.fact: The same continuity underlies the reconstruction of Ermanno A. Arslan, who treats the La Tène migration into Italy as selective.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: To strengthen their forces they hired _____, mercenaries from the Rhône valley
Insubres.fact: To strengthen their forces they hired Gaesatae, mercenaries from the Rhône valley.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: The coalition army, some 50,000 foot and 20,000 horse and chariots, was caught between two _____ forces and destroyed
Insubres.fact: The coalition army, some 50,000 foot and 20,000 horse and chariots, was caught between two Roman forces and destroyed. In 223 BC the Romans attacked the Insubres directly, crossing the Po from the territory of the Anares.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: A first setback drove them back onto the land of their _____ allies, from which they resumed the campaign
Insubres.fact: At the Battle of Telamon in 225 BC the Cenomani and Veneti sided with Rome, which obliged the Insubres and Boii to leave part of their men to defend their own land. A first setback drove them back onto the land of their Cenomani allies, from which they resumed the campaign.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: The following year their request for peace was refused by the consuls _____ and Gnaeus Cornelius Scipio, and they hired a further 30,000 Gaesatae
Insubres.fact: The following year their request for peace was refused by the consuls Marcus Claudius Marcellus and Gnaeus Cornelius Scipio, and they hired a further 30,000 Gaesatae.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: The Romans opened the campaign of 222 BC with the siege of _____, a stronghold near the confluence of the Adda and the Po
Insubres.fact: The Romans opened the campaign of 222 BC with the siege of Acerrae, a stronghold near the confluence of the Adda and the Po. Acerrae and then Mediolanum fell, which forced the Insubres to surrender.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: In the ensuing battle _____ relieved the place, killing the Gaesatic commander Britomartus in single combat and winning the spolia opima
Insubres.fact: The following year their request for peace was refused by the consuls Marcus Claudius Marcellus and Gnaeus Cornelius Scipio, and they hired a further 30,000 Gaesatae. In the ensuing battle Marcellus relieved the place, killing the Gaesatic commander Britomartus in single combat and winning the spolia opima.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: Rome meanwhile founded the colonies of _____ and Cremona in 218 BC to control the Po where it divided the two great Gallic peoples
Insubres.fact: Rome meanwhile set up the colonies of Placentia and Cremona in 218 BC to control the Po where it divided the two great Gallic peoples. Led by the Carthaginian officer Hamilcar, they took Placentia and Cremona in 201 BC but were defeated before the latter the next year.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: After the Battle of the _____ in 207 BC, the struggle for the Po plain went on for a decade
Insubres.fact: After the Battle of the Metaurus in 207 BC, the struggle for the Po plain went on for a decade.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: Led by the _____ officer Hamilcar, they took Placentia and Cremona in 201 BC but were defeated before the latter the next year
Insubres.fact: Led by the Carthaginian officer Hamilcar, they took Placentia and Cremona in 201 BC but were defeated before the latter the next year.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: They kept a formal independence as a federated state, though their eastern frontier was probably brought back from the Oglio to the Adda for the benefit of _____
Insubres.fact: Led by the Carthaginian officer Hamilcar, they took Placentia and Cremona in 201 BC but were defeated before the latter the next year. They kept a formal independence as a federated state, though their eastern frontier was probably brought back from the Oglio to the Adda for the benefit of Cremona.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: Kruta attributes the difference to their native roots, the elimination of the _____ amounting to a return to the situation before the invasion of the early 4th century BC
Insubres.fact: The Insubres were treated more leniently than the Boii, who were exterminated, enslaved or driven out. Kruta attributes the difference to their native roots, the elimination of the Boii amounting to a return to the situation before the invasion of the early 4th century BC.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: In his reading, the legal use of these Roman categories in turn gave the _____ peoples a new sense of ethnic identity
Insubres.fact: In his reading, the legal use of these Roman categories in turn gave the Transpadane peoples a new sense of ethnic identity. Like the other Transpadane peoples the Insubres passed through a Gallo-Roman period in the 2nd and 1st centuries BC.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: The town stood on a site already occupied in the _____ period
Insubres.fact: The town stood on a site already occupied in the Golasecca period.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: Polybius mentions a federal sanctuary of a war goddess, whom he equates with _____, in which the gold standards called immovable were kept in peacetime, and which the context places at Mediolanum
Insubres.fact: Polybius mentions a federal sanctuary of a war goddess, whom he equates with Athena, in which the gold standards called immovable were kept in peacetime, and which the context places at Mediolanum.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: The sieges of _____ and Mediolanum show that both were fortified places of some size
Insubres.fact: The sieges of Acerrae and Mediolanum show that both were fortified places of some size. In the Transpadane plain the political unity of a Gallic people rested on a capital such as Mediolanum and on strategic centers such as Acerrae, a pattern that contrasts with the dispersed, village-based settlement of the plain south of the Po.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: From about 100 BC the coins carry legends in the _____ alphabet, among them rikos (from rix, 'king') and toutiopouos, concentrated in Insubrian territory
Insubres.fact: From about 100 BC the coins carry legends in the Lepontic alphabet, among them rikos (from rix, 'king') and toutiopouos, concentrated in Insubrian territory.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: A hoard from _____ contained some 1,400 toutiopouos coins
Insubres.fact: A hoard from Manerbio contained some 1,400 toutiopouos coins.

Insubres.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insubres.question: Their epigraphy, on stone, on pottery and on coins, is the richest body of texts directly recorded by a _____ people before the 1st century BC
Insubres.fact: Their epigraphy, on stone, on pottery and on coins, is the richest body of texts directly recorded by a Celtic people before the 1st century BC.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The _____ was Post-Roman British and Irish style of art.
Insular art.fact: Insular art, also called Hiberno-Saxon art, was produced in the post-Roman era of Great Britain and Ireland. Art historians usually group Insular art as part of the Migration Period art movement as well as Early Medieval Western art, and it is the combination of these two traditions that gives the style its special character.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The term derives from insula, the Latin term for "island"; in this period _____ and Ireland shared a largely common style different from that of the rest of Europe
Insular art.fact: Insular art, also called Hiberno-Saxon art, was produced in the post-Roman era of Great Britain and Ireland. The term derives from insula, the Latin term for "island"; in this period Britain and Ireland shared a largely common style different from that of the rest of Europe.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: One major distinctive feature is interlace decoration, in particular the interlace decoration as found at _____, in East Anglia
Insular art.fact: One major distinctive feature is interlace decoration, in particular the interlace decoration as found at Sutton Hoo, in East Anglia.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: This is now applied to decorating new types of objects mostly copied from the _____ world, above all the codex or book
Insular art.fact: This is now applied to decorating new types of objects mostly copied from the Mediterranean world, above all the codex or book.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The finest period of the style was brought to an end by the disruption to monastic centres and aristocratic life caused by the _____ raids which began in the late 8th century
Insular art.fact: The finest period of the style was brought to an end by the disruption to monastic centres and aristocratic life caused by the Viking raids which began in the late 8th century.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: These are presumed to have interrupted work on the Book of Kells; no later _____ books are as heavily or finely illuminated as the masterpieces of the 8th century
Insular art.fact: These are presumed to have interrupted work on the Book of Kells; no later Gospel books are as heavily or finely illuminated as the masterpieces of the 8th century.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: In England the style merged into Anglo-Saxon art around 900, whilst in _____ the style continued until the 12th century, when it merged into Romanesque art
Insular art.fact: In England the style merged into Anglo-Saxon art around 900, whilst in Ireland the style continued until the 12th century, when it merged into Romanesque art. Ireland, Scotland and the kingdom of Northumbria in Northern England are the most important centres, but examples were found also in southern England, Wales and in Continental Europe, especially Gaul (modern France), in centres set up by the Hiberno-Scottish mission and Anglo-Saxon missions.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The best examples include the Book of Kells, _____, Book of Durrow, brooches such as the Tara Brooch and the Ruthwell Cross
Insular art.fact: The best examples include the Book of Kells, Lindisfarne Gospels, Book of Durrow, brooches such as the Tara Brooch and the Ruthwell Cross.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: C. R. Dodwell, on the other hand, says that in Ireland "the Insular style continued almost unchallenged until the Anglo-Norman invasion of _____; indeed examples of it occur even as late as the thirte
Insular art.fact: C. R. Dodwell, on the other hand, says that in Ireland "the Insular style continued almost unchallenged until the Anglo-Norman invasion of 1170; indeed examples of it occur even as late as the thirteenth and fourteenth centuri.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: Late Iron Age Celtic art or "_____ Tène", gave the love of spirals, triskeles, circles and other geometric motifs
Insular art.fact: Late Iron Age Celtic art or "Ultimate La Tène", gave the love of spirals, triskeles, circles and other geometric motifs.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: These were combined with animal forms probably mainly deriving from the _____ version of the general Eurasian animal style, though also from Celtic art, where heads terminating scrolls were common
Insular art.fact: These were combined with animal forms probably mainly deriving from the Germanic version of the general Eurasian animal style, though also from Celtic art, where heads terminating scrolls were common.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The origins of the overall format of the carpet page have often been related to Roman floor mosaics, _____ carpets and manuscript paintings, without general agreement being reached among scholars
Insular art.fact: Interlace was used by both these traditions, as well as Roman art (for example in floor mosaics) and other possible influences such as Coptic art, and its use was taken to new levels in Insular art, where it was combined with the other elements already mentioned. The origins of the overall format of the carpet page have often been related to Roman floor mosaics, Coptic carpets and manuscript paintings, without general agreement being reached among scholars.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: Especially in _____, the clerical and secular elites were often very closely linked; some Irish abbacies were held for generations among a small kin-group
Insular art.fact: Especially in Ireland, the clerical and secular elites were often very closely linked; some Irish abbacies were held for generations among a small kin-group. Ireland was divided into very small "kingdoms", almost too many for historians to keep track of, whilst in Britain there was a smaller number of generally larger kingdoms.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: Ireland was divided into very small "kingdoms", almost too many for historians to keep track of, whilst in _____ there was a smaller number of generally larger kingdoms
Insular art.fact: Ireland was divided into very small "kingdoms", almost too many for historians to keep track of, whilst in Britain there was a smaller number of generally larger kingdoms.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: Both the Celtic (Irish and _____) and Anglo-Saxon elites had long traditions of metalwork of the finest quality, much of it used for the personal adornment of both sexes of the elite
Insular art.fact: Both the Celtic (Irish and Pictish) and Anglo-Saxon elites had long traditions of metalwork of the finest quality, much of it used for the personal adornment of both sexes of the elite.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The Insular style arises from the meeting of their two styles, Celtic and Anglo-Saxon animal style, in a _____ context, and with some awareness of Late Antique style
Insular art.fact: The Insular style arises from the meeting of their two styles, Celtic and Anglo-Saxon animal style, in a Christian context, and with some awareness of Late Antique style.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The role of the _____ of Northumbria in the formation of the new style appears to have been pivotal
Insular art.fact: The role of the Kingdom of Northumbria in the formation of the new style appears to have been pivotal. The northernmost Anglo-Saxon kingdom continued to expand into areas with Celtic populations, but often leaving those populations largely intact in areas such as Dál Riata, Elmet and the Kingdom of Strathclyde.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The Irish monastery at Iona was established by _____ (Colum Cille) in 563, when Iona was part of a Dál Riata that included territory in both Ireland and modern Scotland
Insular art.fact: The Irish monastery at Iona was set up by Saint Columba (Colum Cille) in 563, when Iona was part of a Dál Riata that included territory in both Ireland and modern Scotland.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The majority of examples that survive from the _____ period have been found in archaeological contexts that suggest they were rapidly hidden, lost or abandoned
Insular art.fact: Although the first conversion of a Northumbrian king, that of Edwin in 627, was effected by clergy from the Gregorian Mission to Kent, it was the Celtic Christianity of Iona that was initially more influential in Northumbria, founding Lindisfarne on the eastern coast as a satellite in 635. The majority of examples that survive from the Christian period have been found in archaeological contexts that suggest they were rapidly hidden, lost or abandoned.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: There are a number of large penannular brooches, including several of comparable quality to the _____ brooch
Insular art.fact: There are a number of large penannular brooches, including several of comparable quality to the Tara brooch.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: Almost all of these are in the _____, the National Museum of Ireland, the National Museum of Scotland, or local museums in the islands
Insular art.fact: Almost all of these are in the British Museum, the National Museum of Ireland, the National Museum of Scotland, or local museums in the islands.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: Coloured glass, enamel and millefiori glass, probably imported, are also used, as seen in the late 6th century _____
Insular art.fact: Coloured glass, enamel and millefiori glass, probably imported, are also used, as seen in the late 6th century Ballinderry Brooch.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The Insular crozier had a distinctive shape; the survivals, such as the _____ and Lismore Crozier all appear to be Irish or Scottish, and from rather late in the Insular period
Insular art.fact: The Insular crozier had a distinctive shape; the survivals, such as the Kells Crozier and Lismore Crozier all appear to be Irish or Scottish, and from rather late in the Insular period.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: These later works, which also including the 11th century _____ and Clonmacnoise Croziers are heavily influenced by Viking art and have interlace patterns in the Ringerike or Urnes styles
Insular art.fact: These later works, which also including the 11th century River Laune and Clonmacnoise Croziers are heavily influenced by Viking art and have interlace patterns in the Ringerike or Urnes styles.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The Cross of _____ is a 12th-century Irish processional cross and reliquary that shows Insular decoration, possibly added in a deliberately revivalist spirit
Insular art.fact: The Cross of Cong is a 12th-century Irish processional cross and reliquary that shows Insular decoration, possibly added in a deliberately revivalist spirit.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The book was recovered, but not the cover, as also happened with the Book of _____
Insular art.fact: The book was recovered, but not the cover, as also happened with the Book of Lindisfarne.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The cloisonné enamel shows _____ influence, and is not found in work from the Insular homelands, but the overall effect is very like a carpet page
Insular art.fact: The cloisonné enamel shows Italian influence, and is not found in work from the Insular homelands, but the overall effect is very like a carpet page.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: It contains only decorated letters, at the beginning of each _____, but these already show distinctive traits
Insular art.fact: It contains only decorated letters, at the beginning of each Psalm, but these already show distinctive traits.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: From the same scriptorium and of similar date, the _____ has the earliest carpet page, although a relatively simple one
Insular art.fact: From the same scriptorium and of similar date, the Bobbio Orosius has the earliest carpet page, although a relatively simple one.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The earliest painted Insular manuscript to survive, produced in _____ c
Insular art.fact: The earliest painted Insular manuscript to survive, produced in Lindisfarne c.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: This introduces interlace, and also uses _____ motifs drawn from metalwork
Insular art.fact: This introduces interlace, and also uses Celtic motifs drawn from metalwork.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: Its date and place of origin remain subjects of debate, with 650–690 and Durrow in _____, Iona or Lindisfarne being the normal contenders
Insular art.fact: Its date and place of origin remain subjects of debate, with 650–690 and Durrow in Ireland, Iona or Lindisfarne being the normal contenders.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The influences on the decoration are also highly controversial, especially regarding Coptic or other _____ influence
Insular art.fact: The influences on the decoration are also highly controversial, especially regarding Coptic or other Near Eastern influence.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The figures are highly stylised, and some pages use _____ interlaced animal ornament, whilst others use the full repertoire of Celtic geometric spirals
Insular art.fact: The figures are highly stylised, and some pages use Germanic interlaced animal ornament, whilst others use the full repertoire of Celtic geometric spirals.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The gospels of _____ and Mark and the beginning of Luke survives
Insular art.fact: The gospels of Matthew and Mark and the beginning of Luke survives.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: From its time in Wales, pages include marginalia representing some of the earliest examples of _____ writing
Insular art.fact: From its time in Wales, pages include marginalia representing some of the earliest examples of Old Welsh writing.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The manuscript has been at _____ since the late 10th century, except for a brief period during the English Civil War
Insular art.fact: The manuscript has been at Lichfield Cathedral since the late 10th century, except for a brief period during the English Civil War.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: Attributed to Monkwearmouth-_____ in Northumbria between about 730–746, this contains larger opening letters in which metalwork styles of decoration can clearly be seen
Insular art.fact: Attributed to Monkwearmouth-Jarrow Abbey in Northumbria between about 730–746, this contains larger opening letters in which metalwork styles of decoration can clearly be seen.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: It also contains the earliest historiated initial, a bust probably of _____ I, which like some other elements of the decoration, clearly derives from a Mediterranean model
Insular art.fact: It also contains the earliest historiated initial, a bust probably of Pope Gregory I, which like some other elements of the decoration, clearly derives from a Mediterranean model.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: Book of _____ dated to around 800, although sometimes up to a century earlier, the place of origin is disputed between Iona and Kells, or other locations
Insular art.fact: Book of Kells Usually dated to around 800, although sometimes up to a century earlier, the place of origin is disputed between Iona and Kells, or other locations.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: A few scenes such as the _____ and Arrest of Christ are included, as well as a Madonna and Child, surrounded by angels (the earliest Madonna in a Western book)
Insular art.fact: A few scenes such as the Temptation and Arrest of Christ are included, as well as a Madonna and Child, surrounded by angels (the earliest Madonna in a Western book).

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The Book of Kells is held in _____
Insular art.fact: The Book of Kells is held in Trinity College Dublin. A lesser known Insular manuscript in Trinity College Dublin's library is the Garland of Howth, which is in a damaged condition.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: A lesser known Insular manuscript in _____'s library is the Garland of Howth, which is in a damaged condition
Insular art.fact: The Book of Kells is held in Trinity College Dublin. A lesser known Insular manuscript in Trinity College Dublin's library is the Garland of Howth, which is in a damaged condition.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: Its beautifully tooled goatskin cover is the oldest _____ bookbinding to survive, and a virtually unique example of Insular leatherwork, in an excellent state of preservation
Insular art.fact: Its beautifully tooled goatskin cover is the oldest Western bookbinding to survive, and a virtually unique example of Insular leatherwork, in an excellent state of preservation.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The 8th-century _____ shows mixed elements in the decoration, as does the Stockholm Codex Aureus of similar period, probably written in Canterbury
Insular art.fact: The 8th-century Cotton Bede shows mixed elements in the decoration, as does the Stockholm Codex Aureus of similar period, probably written in Canterbury.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: In the _____ it is clear which element is coming to dominate
Insular art.fact: In the Vespasian Psalter it is clear which element is coming to dominate.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: Many continental manuscripts, especially in areas influenced by the _____ missions, also show such features well into the early Romanesque period
Insular art.fact: Many continental manuscripts, especially in areas influenced by the Celtic missions, also show such features well into the early Romanesque period.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The "most tenacious of all the _____ styles", it continued until as late as the 11th century
Insular art.fact: "Franco-Saxon" is a term for a school of late Carolingian illumination in north-eastern France that used Insular-style decoration, including super-large initials, sometimes in combination with figurative images typical of contemporary French styles. The "most tenacious of all the Carolingian styles", it continued until as late as the 11th century.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: Later Insular carvings found throughout _____ and Ireland were almost entirely geometrical, as was the decoration on the earliest crosses
Insular art.fact: Later Insular carvings found throughout Britain and Ireland were almost entirely geometrical, as was the decoration on the earliest crosses.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The 10th-century Muiredach's _____ at Monasterboice is usually regarded as the peak of the Irish crosses
Insular art.fact: The 10th-century Muiredach's High Cross at Monasterboice is usually regarded as the peak of the Irish crosses.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: In later examples the figures become fewer and larger, and their style begins to merge with the Romanesque, as at the _____ in Ireland
Insular art.fact: In later examples the figures become fewer and larger, and their style begins to merge with the Romanesque, as at the Dysert Cross in Ireland.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The 8th-century _____, unfortunately damaged by Presbyterian iconoclasm, is the most impressive remaining Anglo-Saxon cross, though as with most Anglo-Saxon crosses the original cross head is missing
Insular art.fact: The 8th-century Northumbrian Ruthwell Cross, unfortunately damaged by Presbyterian iconoclasm, is the most impressive remaining Anglo-Saxon cross, though as with most Anglo-Saxon crosses the original cross head is missing.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: Even early Anglo-Saxon examples mix vine-scroll decoration of _____ origin with interlace panels, and in later ones the former type becomes the norm, just as in manuscripts
Insular art.fact: Even early Anglo-Saxon examples mix vine-scroll decoration of Continental origin with interlace panels, and in later ones the former type becomes the norm, just as in manuscripts.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: There are remains of other works of monumental sculpture in Anglo-Saxon art, even from the earlier periods, but nothing comparable from _____
Insular art.fact: There are remains of other works of monumental sculpture in Anglo-Saxon art, even from the earlier periods, but nothing comparable from Ireland.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The carvings come from both pagan and early _____ periods, and the Pictish symbols, which are still poorly understood, do not seem to have been repugnant to Christians
Insular art.fact: The carvings come from both pagan and early Christian periods, and the Pictish symbols, which are still poorly understood, do not seem to have been repugnant to Christians.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: The surviving items from both are now held by the _____ of Scotland
Insular art.fact: The surviving items from both are now held by the National Museum of Scotland.

Insular art.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular art.question: Unmistakable Insular influence can be seen in _____ manuscripts, even though these were also trying to copy the Imperial styles of Rome and Byzantium
Insular art.fact: Unmistakable Insular influence can be seen in Carolingian manuscripts, even though these were also trying to copy the Imperial styles of Rome and Byzantium.

Insular Danish.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular Danish.question: They are recorded in the Dictionary of Danish Insular Dialects (Ømålsordbogen) which has been collected since the 1920s, and published in biannual volumes since _____
Insular Danish.fact: They are recorded in the Dictionary of Danish Insular Dialects (Ømålsordbogen) which has been collected since the 1920s, and published in biannual volumes since 1992.

Insular Danish.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular Danish.question: A major difference between _____ and the traditional insular dialects is that some of them lack the stød but kept the tonal accent
Insular Danish.fact: A major difference between Modern Danish and the traditional insular dialects is that some of them lack the stød but kept the tonal accent.

Insular Danish.subject: Environment & Ecology
Insular Danish.question: By _____, Zealand insular dialects had been reduced to two genders under the influence from the standard language, but other varieties like Funen dialect had not
Insular Danish.fact: By 1900, Zealand insular dialects had been reduced to two genders under the influence from the standard language, but other varieties like Funen dialect had not.
